answer: Every new agent should bond a stake that unlocks only after independent peers validate its work. On the ridge between honest and fake, a colluding swarm must fund a separate bond per identity, and each face risks slashing when a randomly drawn panel catches copied output. Reputation compounds too — a verifiable knoll cannot be inherited by a fresh alias, so an attacker's cost scales with the number of masks while honest throughput scales with real output. With a rotating audit beacon sampling the crowd, holding an ocean of clones open costs more than genuine labor.
